items.label: A
items.critique: The screaming 'Gahhhhhh!', the half-blind hermit mistaking the hero, '?!' and 'Oh....' punctuation and a reward scroll 'about bats' are Westwood's comic touch.

items.label: B
items.critique: Overwrought exclamations ('for the darkest purposes, indeed!'), 'that foul demoness' and a teasing 'sooner than you think' reward line; masked names everywhere, a bare journal.

items.label: C
items.critique: Well shaped, but the offer explains why the horn matters in a neat sentence, ends 'What say you?', and the reminder is an atmospheric mood line instead of a nudge.

items.label: D
items.critique: Long breathless setup with odd logic (can't leave or the wolf-wife runs off), 'What are you waiting for?' and a vague 'token of our appreciation': classic campaign.

items.label: E
items.critique: Panicky, low-stakes family worry ('he'll be destroyed'), the hesitant 'Could you... would you', generic thanks and a journal precise about place: Westwood's side-quest voice.

items.label: F
items.critique: Invented magic object explained in one tidy clause ('burns without wood'), stakes stated, location given, and a reward counted in exact gold from the Captain's purse.

items.label: G
items.critique: Plot-carrying main-quest text with double-hyphen dash, 'at whatever the cost!', a death reported offhand and a handoff to the next chapter; uneven but authentic.

items.label: H
items.critique: Charming, but the enchanted honey crock gets the same one-line mechanic gloss, and 'Your supper's on the house' is a cosier humour than Nox's.

items.label: I
items.critique: Mannered academic register ('most regrettable position', 'does not forget its benefactors', 'undertake to recover') is too literary for Nox's plain speakers.

items.label: J
items.critique: Same template: snatched object, what it magically does, where the thieves went, 'Would you go after them, lad?', exact '80 gold' reward.

tells: New offers follow a fixed template: the theft, a one-clause explanation of the object's magic or importance, the exact place the thief went, then a closing question to the hero. Westwood's offers wander, carry plot, or have odd logic.
New rewards are counted (80 gold, 100 gold) or tied to a titled NPC (the Captain sends...). Westwood's thanks are generic ('take this as a token of my appreciation') or a named item/spell.
New objects are invented, homely magic gadgets (fire-stone, honey crock, dowsing rod) that need a gloss; Westwood's items are masked proper nouns or plain things (spectacles, staff, cloak).
Westwood leans on overwrought punctuation ('?!', 'Oh....', '--', 'indeed!') and stock epithets ('brave Adventurer', 'foul demoness'); new texts are cleaner and more evenly paced.
A raised or literary register (scholarly understatement, 'What say you?') gives new texts away; Nox's speakers are plain and a little melodramatic.
